autotest: add a package of Bluetooth LE HID sanity tests The sanity package name is bluetooth_AdapterLEHIDSanity.py. The test is written as a package of tests in order to reduce test time, since auto-test ramp up time per test is costy. Between each two tests, the method _cleanup_and_restart is called to restart both peer and DUT. The HID device type (e.g. mouse or keyboard) can be selected per test using this method. At the end of each test, the method _update_test_result is called to track test results. At the end of the package, _print_test_results is called to print a summary of the test results. The test package contains 3 tests at this point - _test_connect_disconnect_loop _test_mouse_reports _test_auto_reconnect Test command example: test_that --autotest_dir ~/trunk/src/third_party/autotest/files/ --args "chameleon_host=<IP Fizz>" <IP DUT> bluetooth_AdapterLEHIDSanity To setup nrf52 device, please refer to - src/third_party/autotest-private/nRF52/ble_app_hids/README BUG=chromium:949394 TEST=running the test on eve device Change-Id: If69152f50907faa4c4b1a154722c2d08b46b39b0 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1551975 Commit-Ready: Yoni Shavit <yshavit@chromium.org> Tested-by: Yoni Shavit <yshavit@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Shyh-In Hwang <josephsih@chromium.org>

cryptohome: Remove precomputed salt challenge-response signature Remove the codepath that allowed to pass precomputed salt signature to the challenge-response vault keyset decryption operation. For the background, this codepath was originally added to allow for an optimization of the vault keyset decryption operation immediately after its creation - so that we're doing only one challenge-response for decrypting the TPM-protected secret, and reuse the salt's signature obtained during the creation step. This codepath won't be useful anymore, since the recent changes in the encryption algorithms (e.g., crrev.com/c/1524781) allow not doing a decryption operation when the vault keyset is created. BUG=chromium:806788 TEST=existing unit tests ChallengeCredentialsDecryptOperation*Test Change-Id: I20ade9d535f55ca33399a3da36a4da194250e6fd Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1557814 Commit-Ready: Maksim Ivanov <emaxx@chromium.org> Tested-by: Maksim Ivanov <emaxx@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org>

power: Use CLOCK_BOOTTIME for BatteryDischargeRate UMA. Currently we use wall clock time for logging BatteryDischargeRateWhileSuspended UMA metrics. This can produce spurious values in scenarios such as daylight savings where the Wall clock time can move backward. Instead use the CLOCK_BOOTTIME that increases monotonically even when the system is supended. BUG=None TEST=unittests pass. Change-Id: Ie3630dca36d5436bb109c1f03852bd8543eeba48 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1558811 Commit-Ready: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org> Tested-by: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org>

ish: solve timer reliability and time jumps b:129805553 demonstrates that the time jumps by 2^32 us twice during boot. This appears to have been caused by leftover interrupts that have not been cleared while the system was booting triggering T0. In addition, b:124890290 discusses that the LRE bit should not be set in HPET configuration, and the do-while loop introduced in CL:1457597 is no longer needed if the settling spin-lock is placed before arming the timer. This resolves that BRANCH=none BUG=b:124890290,b:12980553 TEST=timer appears to be working reliably for 24 hours on arcada, no time jumps Change-Id: Ib0c6b8c9c7e8fe2111a312b9c48061b296178c72 Signed-off-by: Jack Rosenthal <jrosenth@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1548505 Reviewed-by: Jett Rink <jettrink@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Paul Fagerburg <pfagerburg@chromium.org>
